steps.name: Sample structure QC
caveats: Sample labels in counts.csv must be matched to metadata.csv by exact name before plotting; report any mismatch instead of guessing
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-with-covariates-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples; gene ID column + 12 sample columns; Salmon gene-level counts as delivered) and /eval-four-models-v2-with-covariates-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows: sample, condition, sex, age). Design: 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. The groups are not matched on age, and sex and age are the covariates of the downstream design, so report the per-group age distributions.
steps.question: Do the 12 adipose samples (6 treated, 6 control) separate by condition in a blind variance-stabilized expression space, and is any sample worth flagging (outlier, low library size, possible identity swap) before the differential expression test?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes per R-0033@40bf

constraints: qc_sample_structure: transform = vst_blind (vst blind to the design; doi:10.12688/f1000research.7035.1)
qc_sample_structure: n_top_genes = 500 (PCA on the top 500 highly variable genes)
Color all plots by condition (treated/control) and by sex, and print the per-group age range, since the groups are not matched on age
Flag, but do not remove, any sample that departs from its group, and state the reason
steps.description: Blind variance-stabilizing transform, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, Euclidean sample-distance heatmap, all colored by condition (and by sex), plus a per-sample table of library size, sex, and age.
acceptance_criteria: PCA plot and sample-distance heatmap saved, colored by condition, with sample labels consistent with metadata.csv
Per-sample library-size table reported; any sample with a library size far below the median is flagged
Per-group age ranges reported and the treated-vs-control age distributions described
An explicit statement of which samples, if any, are flagged and why, or 'no sample flagged'

steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log fold change shrinkage
caveats: The quantifier name alone does not establish that a length correction occurred: with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the length offset is lost and a change in isoform use can show as differential expression; state this in the plan and in the report. Do not run tximport on a gene table and do not invent a length input.

With 6 samples per condition cell, DESeq2 flags count outliers by Cook's distance and sets the p-value and padj of those genes to NA instead of replacing the count; report those genes separately from the genes dropped by independent filtering.
If the row identifiers of counts.csv are not gene symbols, annotate them to symbols with org.Hs.eg.db (installed) and carry both IDs in the output table.
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-with-covariates-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples) and /eval-four-models-v2-with-covariates-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (sample, condition, sex, age). The count table is gene-level from Salmon; no per-sample quantification files (quant.sf / abundance.h5) and no average transcript length table were delivered, so the length correction is not established: fit the negative-binomial count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset (R-0169). If the matrix is non-integer (fractional Salmon estimates), report that and let DESeq2 apply its standard non-integer-counts handling; do not silently floor or round yourself, and do not run tximport on a gene table. Design: ~ sex + age + condition; condition is a factor explicitly relevelled with 'control' as the reference; sex is a factor; age is the continuous covariate, centered on its grand mean before the fit (the centered column enters the design). Contrast: c('condition','treated','control'), so positive log2FC means higher expression in treated.
steps.question: Which genes differ in expression between treated and control, with the treatment contrast adjusted for sex and age?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log fold change shrinkage per R-0029@22ca

constraints: filter_low_counts: filter_policy = minimal_then_independent (doi:10.1073/pnas.0914005107)
filter_low_counts: min_count = 10 (doi:10.12688/f1000research.7035.1)
filter_low_counts: min_samples = smallest_group_size (6) (vignette:DESeq2/1.52.0#pre-filtering)
normalize: size_factors = median_of_ratios_named_in_the_plan (DESeq2 size factors; no pre-normalizing or transforming the counts before the model; doi:10.1186/s13059-014-0550-8)
model_design: import = gene_counts_without_length_offset (doi:10.12688/f1000research.7563.2)
model_design: missing_input = quantification_directories_or_avg_tx_length_table (not available here, hence no length offset; do not run tximport on a gene table and do not invent a length input)
model_design: reference_level = explicit (relevel condition to 'control'; vignette:DESeq2/1.52.0#note-on-factor-levels)
model_design: contrast_form = factor_numerator_denominator (condition: treated vs control; vignette:DESeq2/1.52.0#contrasts)
model_design: covariate_handling = design_terms (sex and age as fixed effects in the design, not removed from the counts; doi:10.12688/f1000research.27893.1)
model_design: continuous_covariate = center_before_the_fit (age; rule:R-0023)
differential_expression: test = Wald (doi:10.1186/s13059-014-0550-8)

differential_expression: count_outlier_policy = flag_and_report_na (keep the default Cook's-distance handling; with 6 replicates per cell, flagged genes get NA p-values and must be reported separately; vignette:DESeq2/1.52.0#approach-to-count-outliers)
shrink_lfc: lfc_shrink = apeglm (doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/bty895)
multiple_testing: independent_filtering = true (doi:10.1073/pnas.0914005107)
multiple_testing: pvalue_histogram = inspect_before_adjustment (save the histogram and describe its shape; doi:10.3390/ht7030023)
multiple_testing: alpha = 0.05 (vignette:DESeq2/1.52.0#independent-filtering-and-multiple-testing)
multiple_testing: adjustment = BH (doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x)

multiple_testing: lfc_threshold_policy = test_against_threshold (doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btp053) - no fold-change threshold is requested for this question, so selection is on the adjusted p-value alone
multiple_testing: filter_results_by = adjusted_pvalue (doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x)
steps.description: DESeqDataSet after the minimal pre-filter (genes with >=10 counts in >=6 samples), DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors, Wald test of the condition contrast adjusted for sex and age, apeglm-shrunken fold changes, and Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p-values at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on. Outputs: the full results table, the p-value histogram, and the key counts.
acceptance_criteria: Results table for all genes passing the pre-filter, with columns baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, shrunken_log2FoldChange
Design matrix has 4 coefficients (Intercept, sex, centered age, condition_treated_vs_control); a positive shrunken log2FoldChange means higher in treated
n_tested, n_DE at FDR 0.05, and the NA p-value counts from outlier flagging and from independent filtering are reported separately
P-value histogram saved with its shape described (flat or decreasing toward 1 is expected)
An explicit statement that counts were modeled as delivered, without a length offset, because the Salmon gene table's length correction is not established

steps.name: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test (robustness)
caveats: edgeR uses TMM normalization factors, not DESeq2 size factors - this is the expected method difference, not a discrepancy to reconcile

test = QLF differs from the sourced DESeq2 Wald default (warning under rule R-0001@9a17); this is deliberate - the two methods are each other's robustness check, and the report presents their overlap, not one method alone
steps.context: Same inputs as T1S2: /eval-four-models-v2-with-covariates-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv and /eval-four-models-v2-with-covariates-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv. Apply the identical pre-filter as T1S2 (>=10 counts in >=6 samples) so both methods test exactly the same genes. DGEList + TMM normalization factors; a design matrix that matches T1S2 exactly (sex factor, centered age, condition with 'control' as reference); glmQLFit on the full design, glmQLFTest on the condition_treated_vs_control coefficient; select at FDR 0.05. This is the second method for robustness (permitted by R-0001@9a17); the primary result is the DESeq2 Wald test from T1S2.
steps.question: Does the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same counts, the same pre-filter, and the same design corroborate the DESeq2 differential gene set?

grounding.reason: Second method for robustness per the T1S2 alternative (edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test, rule R-0001@9a17), run on the same counts, pre-filter, and design as the primary DESeq2 path

constraints: The design matrix must encode the same factors with the same reference levels as the DESeq2 model in T1S2 (condition reference 'control'; age centered identically)
The pre-filter must be identical to T1S2 (>=10 counts in >=6 samples)
Select genes at FDR < 0.05 from the quasi-likelihood F-test on the condition_treated_vs_control coefficient
steps.description: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test of the treatment contrast adjusted for sex and age, plus the overlap table against the T1S2 DESeq2 set (intersection, DESeq2-only, edgeR-only).
acceptance_criteria: DE gene count at FDR 0.05 from the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test
Overlap table against the T1S2 set: intersection size (the high-confidence set), DESeq2-only genes, edgeR-only genes - the union is never presented as the result
Statement that the gene set and the design matched T1S2 exactly

steps.name: Report
steps.context: Inputs: the T1S2 results table (baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, shrunken_log2FoldChange) and the T1S3 edgeR table with its overlap. Assemble: (1) the MA plot (DE genes marked) and the dispersion plot before the gene tables, each with a one-line statement of what it shows; (2) the p-value histogram with its shape described; (3) the gene table with log2FoldChange, shrunken_log2FoldChange (name the estimator: apeglm), and lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken log2FoldChange - never by the unshrunken value - with p-values from the unshrunken fit; (4) n_tested, n_DE per method, and the two-method overlap: the intersection is the high-confidence set, method-only genes are listed with the method name, and the union is never presented as the result; (5) report fields: method, package versions, design formula (~ sex + age + condition), contrast (condition: treated vs control), thresholds (padj < 0.05; no fold-change threshold requested), n_tested, n_de, sessionInfo, seed; (6) the explicit statement that counts were modeled without a length offset because the Salmon gene table's length correction is not established, so a change in isoform use can show as differential expression.
steps.question: Assemble the differential expression report: which genes differ between treated and control adjusted for sex and age, how robust is the set across the two methods, what do the fit diagnostics show, and what are the stated limitations?
constraints: report: effect_columns = log2FoldChange, shrunken_log2FoldChange, lfcSE (doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/bty895)
report: rank_genes_by = shrunken_log2FoldChange (vignette:DESeq2/1.52.0#log-fold-change-shrinkage-for-visualization-and-ranking)
report: fit_diagnostics = ma_plot, dispersion_plot (vignette:DESeq2/1.52.0#ma-plot)
report: robustness = overlap_of_two_methods (doi:10.1261/rna.053959.115)
report: report_fields = method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, session_info (doi:10.1093/bib/bbz124)
report: reproducibility_record = session_info, seed, package_versions, collection_version, annotation_release (doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285)
steps.description: Final report (figures + gene tables + methods and reproducibility block) answering which genes differ between treated and control, adjusted for sex and age.
acceptance_criteria: Report contains the MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram, the ranked gene table with both fold-change columns and lfcSE, n_tested and n_DE per method, the overlap counts, sessionInfo, and the length-offset statement
Genes are ranked by the shrunken log2FoldChange and the p-values are from the unshrunken fit
The high-confidence set is the DESeq2/edgeR intersection, method-only genes are listed with the method name, and the union is not presented as the result

plan.title: Adipose treated vs control DE (sex/age adjusted)
plan.analytical_narrative: Human adipose bulk RNA-seq, 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch; sex and age are recorded per sample and the groups are not matched on age, so the condition contrast is adjusted for both as fixed effects in the design. The Salmon gene-level count table (12000 genes x 12 samples) does not establish the length correction (no per-sample quantification files, no average transcript length table), so per R-0169 the count model is fit on the counts as delivered with no length offset, and the limitation is stated in the report. Flow: (T1S1) sample-structure QC on blind-vst counts to confirm the 12 samples group by condition and flag any outlier before testing; (T1S2) minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples) then DESeq2 negative-binomial Wald test with design ~ sex + age + condition (control reference, age centered), apeglm-shrunken fold changes, Benjamini-Hochberg at FDR 0.05 with independent filtering on; (T1S3) the same counts, filter, and design through the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as the second method, so the report can show the overlap instead of the union; (T1S4) the report: MA and dispersion diagnostics, p-value histogram, gene table ranked by shrunken log2FC, DE counts per method, the two-method overlap, and the reproducibility record.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

DESeq2 minimal pre-filter
DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors inside the negative binomial model
DESeq2 fixed-effects design ~ sex + age + condition
DESeq2 Wald test
apeglm LFC shrinkage on the condition coefficient
Benjamini-Hochberg with independent filtering
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test
